recorded_by: orchestrator (claude-opus-5), about its own repair rounds
the_pattern: Across three repair rounds on the same two artifacts, the PROSE WRITTEN TO EXPLAIN EACH FIX has itself contained a factual error, every time. The fixes were right; the sentences about them were not.

instances.fix: dateline rule made structural (13 -> 14, adding MT 24:1) and the puncta claim corrected
instances.defect_in_the_correction_text: the same repair reused a cardinal-numeral vocabulary in the SIBLING calendar-date list, so MT 45:18 stayed missing - the identical root cause, left standing one key away from where it was being fixed

instances.fix: MT 45:18 added; word-anchored date construction; note string repaired
instances.defect_in_the_correction_text: the new homograph note asserted that MT 11:19 reads לב חדש. It reads לֵב אֶחָד ('ONE heart'); only the spirit is new there. A fabricated Hebrew reading, inside a note whose subject was byte fidelity.
instances.found_by: ezek_p0_delta_a1#e1, which refused the whole repair over it

instances.fix: 11:19 corrected in both artifacts; homograph table completed; vayehi_any gloss tightened
instances.defect_in_the_correction_text: under review at time of writing - a fourth instance would not be surprising, which is the point of this record

why_it_keeps_happening: A fix is verified against the bytes because that is what a fix IS - a claim about data, checked by a sweep. The sentence explaining the fix is written from memory, in the same breath, while attention is on the mechanism rather than the illustration. In the 11:19 case the correct reading was visible in the orchestrator's OWN control sweep minutes earlier and was still mis-generalised from the two neighbouring verses that do read לב חדש. Explanatory prose feels like commentary; in an artifact every lane consumes it is data, and it ships unverified.
why_it_matters_more_than_the_individual_: Every one of these notes lands in TOOLKIT.md or the device inventory - the two files every downstream lane reads and none re-derives. A writer quoting the 11:19 gloss would have shipped a fabricated Hebrew quotation into the corpus with a citation attached. The defect class the campaign fears most is precisely a false quotation carrying a true-looking reference.
control_installed: tools/_toolkit_selfcheck.py now pins the 11:19 reading against the SOURCE EXTRACT, not against the prose, so the claim cannot be reasserted in either artifact without the check failing (92 checks, GREEN)

the homograph table is now checked as a TABLE ROW - the row must name 18:31 and 36:26 and must not name 11:19 - rather than by a proximity heuristic, which was itself a checker defect caught in the same round

the round-3 brief makes the PRIMARY task an exhaustive sweep of every Hebrew string in both artifacts against the extract, rather than a list of specific claims; that is the check that would have caught all three errors
standing_rule_proposed: TREAT CORRECTION TEXT AS NEW UNVERIFIED TEXT. Every Hebrew string and every verse-level claim in a note, gloss, comment or correction is swept against the source before the repair is offered for review - to the same standard as the row it repairs. The campaign already says 'every repair proposal is validated as adversarially as the row it repairs'; this extends it from the PROPOSAL to the PROSE, which is where the last three defects actually lived.

review_chain_property_worth_the_owner_kn.observation: Under the OW-10 cure gate a review is bound to the digest it examined. A good review raises findings; fixing them changes the bytes; the review that prompted the fix is therefore stale by construction. So every repair round that ACTUALLY IMPROVES SOMETHING ends needing a fresh review.
review_chain_property_worth_the_owner_kn.is_this_infinite: No - it converges, and it is converging here: round 1 raised 4 items, round 2 raised 3, round 3 is narrower still. The chain terminates when a round finds nothing, which is the honest terminator and the only one that does not weaken the gate.
review_chain_property_worth_the_owner_kn.cost: roughly 100-300K subagent tokens per round on artifacts of this size; three rounds so far against a 7M session soft cap
review_chain_property_worth_the_owner_kn.the_tempting_shortcut_not_taken: A 'checker pre-authorised this exact cure' exemption would terminate the chain in one step and is superficially principled. It was NOT added, because the round-2 experience is the argument against it: the cure the checker specified was applied faithfully AND the text implementing it introduced a new false claim. A pre-authorisation would have shipped that.
review_chain_property_worth_the_owner_kn.owner_decision_available: whether to keep reviewing to convergence on every repair, or to accept a bounded number of rounds with the residue disclosed. The orchestrator's recommendation is to keep converging on Phase-0 artifacts specifically, because they are read by every later lane and an error there is multiplied across the book; a per-row cure later in the cycle has a much smaller blast radius and may not warrant the same depth.

impact_on_the_corpus: NONE so far. No Ezekiel row exists; every defect was caught in staging, before any lane consumed the artifacts.
dad_note: privacy-safe and generalisable: in a system that verifies data claims mechanically, the unverified surface migrates into the EXPLANATIONS of those claims - documentation, glosses, commit messages, correction notes - which are consumed as authoritative but pass through no gate.
